scl_full

Source: R/scl-full.R
scl_full.Rd

Full spatially-constrained clustering.

scl_full(
  xy,
  dmat,
  ncl,
  linkage = "single",
  shortest = TRUE,
  nnbs = 6L,
  boundary = NULL
)

Arguments

xy

Rectangular structure (matrix, data.frame, tibble), containing coordinates of points to be clustered.

dmat

Structure (matrix, data.frame, tibble) containing distances or equivalent metrics between all points in xy. If xy has n rows, then dmat may either be square, with n rows and n columns, or in long form, with three columns of (from, to, value). In long form, from and to are either integer row indices of xy or character values matching rownames (xy). Values may be given for one direction of each pair only, and are then mirrored; values for all pairs must be present.

ncl

Desired number of clusters. See description of `ncl_iterate` parameter for conditions under which actual number may be less than this value.

linkage

One of "single", "average", or "complete". For covariance clustering, use shortest = FALSE; "complete" linkage then uses the smallest connecting value between clusters. As for scl_redcap, initial clusters are always formed from spatially nearest neighbours; shortest and linkage determine only how these are then merged according to dmat.

shortest

If TRUE, the dmat is interpreted as distances such that lower values indicate stronger relationships, and the tree is cut to minimise the within-cluster sum of squared deviations of dmat values. If FALSE, then higher values of dmat are interpreted to indicate stronger relationships, as is the case for example with covariances, and the tree is cut to maximise the mean dmat value within clusters. This parameter only affects how the tree is cut; it has no effect on construction of the spanning tree, which is always based on spatial distances.

nnbs

Number of spatially nearest neighbours to be used in calculating clustering trees, irrespective of shortest. Triangulation will be used if nnbs <= 0. Ignored if boundary is given.

boundary

Optional boundary of the study region. If given, spatial neighbours are taken from a constrained Delaunay triangulation of the points within this boundary (requires the 'cdtr' package), so that no neighbour edges cross outside it, for example across concavities in the region. May be a two-column matrix or data frame of the vertices of a single ring, a list of such rings (holes are recognised by nesting), or an 'sf' polygon or multipolygon object. All points in xy must lie inside the boundary.

Value

A object of class scl with tree containing the clustering scheme, and xy the original coordinate data of the clustered points. An additional component, tree_rest, enables the tree to be re-cut to a different number of clusters via scl_recluster.

See also

Other clustering_fns: scl_recluster(), scl_redcap()

Examples

n <- 100
xy <- matrix (runif (2 * n), ncol = 2)
dmat <- matrix (runif (n^2), ncol = n)
scl <- scl_full (xy, dmat, ncl = 4)
